stories.headline: Russian Drone Strike Hits Kryvyi Rih Mall in Double-Tap Attack
stories.body:
A Russian double-tap drone strike targeted the largest shopping center in Kryvyi Rih, leaving many dead and injured. News outlets and regional officials gave varying casualty numbers following the attack. The BBC reported that at least 15 people were killed in the strike. In contrast, Al Jazeera reported that 14 people were killed. Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Ganzha also stated that the drone strikes on the Kryvyi Rih shopping centre killed 14 people.

The number of reported injuries from the mall attack also varied across reports. The BBC stated that 130 people were injured, including 23 children, when the drone attack struck Kryvyi Rih's largest mall. Al Jazeera reported that the strike injured over 100 people, including 22 children. Meanwhile, Oleksandr Ganzha stated that the drone strikes wounded 121 others. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that the second wave of the drone strike specifically targeted emergency workers who were responding to the scene.

Russian strikes were reported in other areas of Ukraine as well. Separate Russian attacks in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region killed four people, including three children. In the Kharkiv region, a separate Russian drone strike killed two women, aged 73 and 66, and injured two other people.

Ukrainian forces also conducted drone strikes across the border inside Russia. A Ukrainian drone attack struck a car near Razumnoye in Russia's Belgorod region, killing one person and wounding four others. President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that a Ukrainian drone attack hit an oil refinery in Perm as well as the Marinovka military airfield in Volgograd. Russia's Defence Ministry stated that its air defences intercepted 325 Ukrainian drones over 15 Russian regions and Crimea.

The drone strikes occur as the broader conflict continues. Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Moscow currently controls about a fifth of Ukrainian territory. Meanwhile, international political leaders are preparing for diplomatic discussions regarding Ukraine. The Coalition of the Willing meeting, set to take place on Ukraine's independence day, will be co-chaired by French President Emmanuel Macron, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

stories.headline: Turkey Requests Interpol Arrest Warrants for Israeli Leaders Over Flotilla Raid
stories.body:
Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek announced that Turkey has requested Interpol red notices for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and another suspect. The request relates to an attack in May on the Global Sumud Flotilla. Earlier, on July 14, Turkey issued arrest warrants against 35 people on charges including genocide, crimes against humanity, and torture related to the Gaza aid flotilla interception. Among those named in Turkish arrest warrants is Israeli soldier Afek Moskovitch, who faces charges including genocide and torture. France, Italy, and Australia have also launched judicial proceedings regarding Israel's detention of activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla.

In response to the legal actions, Benjamin Netanyahu's office called Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an antisemitic dictator who massacred Kurds and supports Hamas. Netanyahu's office added that Erdogan's attempt to intimidate Israeli leaders will go nowhere. In a separate regional development, Syria accused Israel of striking a disused military air base located near Aleppo.

stories.headline: Hong Kong Court Convicts Former Tiananmen Vigil Leaders Under Security Law
stories.body:
A panel of three judges in Hong Kong has convicted former Tiananmen vigil organizers Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung for incitement to subversion. Lee Cheuk-yan, aged 69, and Chow Hang-tung, aged 41, face a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison under Hong Kong's national security law. Former Hong Kong lawmaker Albert Ho, who was a co-defendant in the subversion trial, pleaded guilty in January.

The subversion case against their organization, the Hong Kong Alliance, focused on its slogan demanding an end to one-party rule. The Hong Kong Alliance was originally founded in May 1989 to support student pro-democracy rallies in Beijing. Chow Hang-tung previously had her 2022 conviction overturned by Hong Kong's top court regarding a 2021 arrest for inciting the public to join the Tiananmen vigil. While in detention, Chow Hang-tung wrote a letter from prison to UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, urging Britain to adopt a more robust stance against China.

stories.headline: Jailed Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan Sent for Hospital Check-Up
stories.body:
Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was briefly taken to an Islamabad hospital for a court-ordered medical examination before being returned to Adiala Jail hours later. Khan was originally arrested in 2023, sentenced to three years in prison on corruption charges, and disqualified from politics for five years. In January 2025, Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi were sentenced to 14 years and seven years in prison, respectively, in a separate corruption case.

Relatives of Imran Khan stated that he is being subjected to torture in prison. His son Kasim stated in February that Khan had lost most of the vision in his right eye, leaving him with only 15 percent eyesight. Following the latest examination, Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar stated that a team of qualified doctors declared Khan medically fit.

Security concerns altered the medical visit. Imran Khan was transferred to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences instead of the court-ordered private Shifa International Hospital. A senior police official told the BBC that a heavy police presence placed outside Shifa International Hospital was used as a decoy.

stories.headline: UK, Australia, and Canada Condemn Israel Over Halted World Central Kitchen Probe
stories.body:
The UK, Australia, and Canada issued a joint statement calling Israel's decision not to conduct a criminal investigation into an April 2024 strike on a World Central Kitchen convoy shameful. The Israeli drone strike in April 2024 killed seven World Central Kitchen aid workers, including three Britons, an Australian, a Pole, a dual US-Canadian national, and a Palestinian. Following the Israeli military's announcement that it would not pursue criminal investigations into the attack, Poland and Australia summoned Israel's ambassadors. The joint statement noted that 186 humanitarian workers were killed in Gaza in 2025. One of the Israeli military officers dismissed over the convoy strike had previously signed an open letter calling for Gaza to be deprived of humanitarian aid.

In other military announcements, the Israeli military stated it will conduct a criminal investigation into the killing of five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab and six relatives, as well as the March 2025 killing of 15 Palestinians. Meanwhile, UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called Israel's tender for 1,200 settlement homes in the West Bank's E1 area an unacceptable and destructive act. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar rejected Miliband's statement, asserting that Jewish people have the right to live throughout the Land of Israel.

stories.headline: US and Canada Negotiate Trade Deal as Trump Tariff Deadline Looms
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump has threatened to impose a 50 percent tariff on approximately $20 billion worth of Canadian goods starting Saturday at 12:01am EDT. In response, Canadian Minister Dominic LeBlanc met US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer in Washington, DC, for over three hours to negotiate a trade deal. Political pressure is building inside Canada. A Leger Opinion poll showed that 56 percent of Canadians do not want Prime Minister Mark Carney to make further trade concessions to the US. Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew called Donald Trump very weak and urged Canada to fight rather than make concessions. In a leaked audio recording, US Vice President JD Vance mocked Prime Minister Carney for attempting to out-tough Trump.

Tensions over trade have already affected alcohol sales. The White House stated that Canadian imports of US alcohol dropped approximately 81 percent year-on-year following Canadian retaliatory measures. Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston and Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew confirmed that Prime Minister Carney asked Canadian provinces to allow US alcohol back on store shelves.

stories.headline: Rahul Gandhi Stages Sit-In Protest Over Student Pellet Gun Injury in Delhi
stories.body:
Indian political leader Rahul Gandhi staged a seven-hour sit-in protest outside the office of New Delhi's Deputy Commissioner of Police to demand formal police action regarding an injured student. Gandhi's protest demanded a First Information Report, known as an FIR, over severe pellet gun injuries suffered by 19-year-old student Sahil Lochab. During a student march in Delhi on July 20, Sahil Lochab sustained over 200 pellets in his body and lost vision in his right eye. Following Rahul Gandhi's sit-in protest, Delhi Police registered an FIR under Sections 118(1) and 125 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Rahul Gandhi claimed that the final approval to register the FIR came directly from Home Secretary and Union Home Minister Amit Shah.

The police actions taken during the July 20 student protest have drawn conflicting reports and claims from government figures and security forces. A general diary entry recorded at the Sansad Marg police station stated that Rapid Action Force personnel fired two rounds from anti-riot guns. However, an inquiry conducted by the Central Reserve Police Force found that Rapid Action Force personnel actually fired seven pellet rounds. In contrast to reports of severe injuries, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju claimed that no protester was seriously injured or suffered broken bones during the July 20 police action.

Official investigations and political fallout followed the demonstration. The Supreme Court of India constituted a five-member High-Powered Enquiry Committee, headed by a former Supreme Court judge, to investigate the police action during the July 20 protest. The political impact was also felt in the national cabinet, where Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25 following opposition protests over police action against student demonstrators.

Government figures attacked Rahul Gandhi's motivations for staging the demonstration. Union Minister JP Nadda criticized Rahul Gandhi's sit-in as camera-centric drama designed to distract from criticism regarding the national song and flag.

stories.headline: Indian Government Rules Out Ethanol Diversion as Sugar Prices Increase
stories.body:
The Indian government estimated domestic sugar production for the current season at 306 lakh tonnes, which is 11 percent lower than the initial estimate of 343 lakh tonnes. Lower supply contributed to rising costs, with retail sugar prices in India reaching Rs 58.2 per kg, representing a 20 percent increase over the previous month. Regional differences emerged across the country. Odisha registered the highest retail sugar price in India at Rs 64.72 per kg, which is up Rs 17.80 compared to the same date in 2025. International sugar prices also rose, jumping more than 16 percent to $552 per tonne on August 20 from $474 per tonne on June 30.

The government rejected claims that sugar shortages were caused by ethanol production. Official data showed the share of Indian sugar diverted for ethanol production declined from around 12 percent in 2022-23 to around 9 percent in 2025-26. To address the shortage and stabilize domestic prices, the Indian government permitted the duty-free import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar. It also imposed a stock limit of 400 tonnes on sugar dealers from August 1 to November 30. Meanwhile, payment processing remained high, as 97 percent of sugarcane dues for the 2025-26 season had been paid to Indian farmers as of August 20.

stories.headline: Twenty-Two Indian Sailors Safe After Ships Hijacked Off Yemen and Somalia
stories.body:
External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal confirmed that 22 Indian seafarers aboard two hijacked merchant vessels off Yemen and Somalia are safe. The first incident involved the Eritrea-flagged oil products tanker MT Sibu 1. The vessel, carrying 16 Indians among its 20 crew members, was hijacked by six armed pirates off the coast of Yemen on August 20.

The second incident involved the Cameroon-flagged cargo ship MV Lutuf, which was hijacked off Somalia's Puntland coast on August 17. The ship was carrying six Indians among its 10 crew members. During the attack, eight armed pirates carrying AK-47-type weapons boarded the MV Lutuf from two skiffs and forced the crew from the citadel to the bridge. The MV Lutuf was carrying Turkish weapons, communications, and satellite equipment bound for a Turkish military training facility located in Mogadishu. India plays a key role in global maritime shipping, as the 2026 BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report estimates India supplies 311,936 seafarers, making it the second-largest supplier globally.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Cuts Legal Practice Requirement for Entry-Level Indian Judges
stories.body:
The Supreme Court of India ruled in a 2-1 majority that advocates with one year of practice are eligible to apply for entry-level judicial officer posts, reducing the prior three-year requirement. Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice A G Masih formed the majority opinion, while Justice Vinod Chandran dissented.

Under the new rules, candidates applying for Civil Judge recruitment between May 25, 2025, and March 31, 2027, will be deemed to meet the one-year legal practice requirement without needing to provide proof certificates. However, starting April 1, 2027, candidates applying for Civil Judge recruitment must produce a certificate of proof of practice showing participation in effective judicial proceedings.

Once selected, judicial candidates will undergo a mandatory two-year post-selection training period. During their first year of training, candidates will receive fixed emoluments equal to half the salary of magistrates. The comprehensive post-selection judicial training program includes one year at a State judicial academy, six months of clerkship under a Principal District Judge, and six months under a High Court judge.
